title: What are Japan's certified evaluation and faculty development (FD) requirements for universities?
description: Japan's certified evaluation cycle under the School Education Act and the FD and staff training duties in the University Establishment Standards.
shortAnswer: Japanese universities must undergo certified evaluation and accreditation by an organization certified by the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) at least once every seven years, and every five years for professional graduate schools, under article 109 of the School Education Act. Article 11 of the University Establishment Standards requires organized training and research to improve the content and methods of classes, known as faculty development (FD), plus training for faculty, administrative staff and teaching assistants.
keyTakeaways: School Education Act article 109(2) requires institutional certified evaluation at intervals set by Cabinet Order; article 40 of the Enforcement Order sets these at within seven years, and within five years for professional graduate schools.
University Establishment Standards article 11(2) requires universities to conduct organized training and research to improve the content and methods of their classes: the legal basis of FD.
Article 11(1) requires training opportunities for faculty and administrative staff, and article 11(3) requires training for teaching assistants and other instructional support staff.
Graduate schools carry the same duties under article 9-3 of the Graduate School Establishment Standards, which extends FD to research supervision.
Evaluators test FD in practice: NIAD-QE's Standard 2-5 asks whether a system for maintaining and improving the quality of teaching and support staff is in place.
regulator: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) and MEXT-certified evaluation and accreditation organizations, including the National Institution for Academic Degrees and Quality Enhancement of Higher Education (NIAD-QE)
appliesTo: National, public and private universities in Japan
Graduate schools, including professional graduate schools such as law schools
Faculty members, administrative staff, and teaching assistants or other instructional support staff
Presidents, vice presidents and committees responsible for internal quality assurance

sections.heading: What is certified evaluation and accreditation and how often is it required?

blocks.text: Certified evaluation and accreditation (ninsho hyoka) is a mandatory external review of a university's overall education and research, conducted by an organization the Minister has certified. Article 109 of the [School Education Act](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/322AC0000000026) sets it out in layers:

items: **Article 109(1):** every university must assess its own education, research, organization, operations, facilities and equipment, and publish the results.
**Article 109(2):** every university must also undergo certified evaluation of its overall condition at intervals set by Cabinet Order.
**Article 109(3):** universities with professional graduate schools or professional universities must also have those units evaluated on their curriculum, faculty organization and other activities.

**Article 109(5) to (7):** the evaluator determines whether the university conforms to its evaluation standards; universities must strive to obtain a finding of conformity, and if they do not, MEXT must request reports or materials from them.

blocks.text: Article 40 of the [School Education Act Enforcement Order](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/328CO0000000340) fixes the intervals: within seven years for institutional evaluation under article 109(2), and within five years for professional schools under article 109(3). Article 110 governs how MEXT certifies evaluation organizations, including the requirement that a university be given an opportunity to object before results are finalized.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the e-Gov texts as at November 2026; the University Establishment Standards include amendments up to MEXT Ordinance No. 29 of September 4, 2026. NIAD-QE's published university standards are titled 2019-2026, so check which standards an evaluator will apply to visits after that period.

Evaluations are conducted by organizations certified by the Minister, each applying its own evaluation standards, and evaluation is conducted at the university's request. NIAD-QE describes the system on its [certified evaluation and accreditation page](https://www.niad.ac.jp/english/unive/cea/) and states that, as of May 2021, the Minister had certified 15 organizations.

NIAD-QE is certified to evaluate universities, colleges of technology and law schools. Its third round of institutional evaluation of universities began in 2019, following rounds from 2005 to 2012 and 2012 to 2019. Its [university standards](https://www.niad.ac.jp/media/008/201901/NIAD-Standards%20for%20Evaluation.pdf) comprise 27 standards in six areas, and the internal quality assurance standards (2-1 to 2-3) are priority items: a university that needs improvement under Standard 2-1 or 2-2 does not meet NIAD-QE's standards.

sections.heading: Which article of the University Establishment Standards requires FD?

blocks.text: Article 11 of the [University Establishment Standards](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/331M50000080028) (Ministry of Education Ordinance No. 28 of 1956), headed "organized training, etc.," contains the FD obligation and two related training duties.

blocks.caption: The three training duties in article 11 of the University Establishment Standards
head: Paragraph
Who it covers
What it requires
rows: Opportunities for training to acquire the knowledge and skills needed, and to improve their abilities and qualities, so that education and research activities are run appropriately and effectively, plus other necessary measures
Organized training and research to improve the content and methods of the university's classes, aimed at enriching education for students (FD)
Instructional support staff other than faculty
Necessary training for those the university assigns to assist with classes

blocks.text: Article 8(3) defines who is covered by article 11(3): faculty, students and others the university designates to assist with a course, who may take over part of a class under the responsible teacher's plan where sufficient educational effect is expected.

Graduate schools have a parallel duty in article 9-3 of the [Graduate School Establishment Standards](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/349M50000080028), where paragraph 2 covers improving the content and methods of both classes and research supervision.

sections.heading: What qualifications must university faculty hold?

blocks.text: Articles 13 to 17 of the University Establishment Standards set qualification routes for each rank, and every rank above assistant also requires educational ability suitable for university teaching. That second limb links qualification to the FD obligation: an appointment decision must consider teaching ability, not only research.

items: **Professor (article 13):** for example, a doctorate with research achievements, equivalent research achievements, a professional degree with practical achievements in the field, prior service as professor or associate professor, or outstanding knowledge and experience in the field.

**Associate professor (article 14):** any professor route, or prior service as assistant professor, a master's or professional degree, research achievements at a research institute, or excellent knowledge and experience.
**Lecturer (article 15):** anyone eligible as professor or associate professor, or a person with suitable educational ability in a special field.
**Assistant professor (article 16):** for example, a master's or professional degree, or knowledge and experience in the field.

blocks.text: Article 8 also defines basic faculty (kikan kyoin): faculty responsible for curriculum and faculty operations who teach main subjects and either work exclusively at the university or teach at least eight credits a year in that faculty's curriculum. Main subjects are, in principle, assigned to basic faculty.

sections.heading: How do evaluators test FD and staff development?

blocks.text: Evaluators look for a functioning system rather than a list of seminars. Under NIAD-QE's Standard 2-5, the decision depends on rules for the employment and promotion of teaching staff (including evaluation of the competencies required), a system for evaluating academic staff performance, systematic initiatives to improve teaching skills, and training for support staff and teaching assistants.

Standard 3-4 separately asks whether cooperation between academic and administrative staff is in place and initiatives to enhance their competencies are carried out. Area Six covers academic programs and learning outcomes, so FD that changes how a course is taught should be visible in the evidence of what students learn. The approach in [how to evidence training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator) translates directly.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each program's degree-level learning outcomes to courses and assessment points, so FD activity can be targeted at the outcomes where evidence shows students fall short. The same map gives evaluators a traceable line from class improvement to learning outcomes under internal quality assurance.

faqs.q: Is FD legally mandatory for Japanese universities?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 11(2) of the University Establishment Standards states that a university shall conduct organized training and research to improve the content and methods of its classes in order to enrich education for students. The Graduate School Establishment Standards impose the same duty on graduate schools in article 9-3, including research supervision.

faqs.q: What happens if a university fails certified evaluation?
faqs.a: Article 109 of the School Education Act requires universities to strive to obtain a finding that they conform to the evaluator's standards. If a university does not obtain that finding, MEXT must request reports or materials from it about its education and research.

faqs.q: Can a university choose which organization evaluates it?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 109 provides that certified evaluation is conducted at the university's request, according to the evaluation standards of the certified organization. Each certified organization sets its own standards and methods, which must satisfy the certification criteria in article 110. NIAD-QE is one of several certified organizations.

faqs.q: Do teaching assistants need training before they help teach?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 11(3) of the University Establishment Standards requires universities to provide necessary training to instructional support staff other than faculty. Under article 8(3), those staff may take over part of a class only under the responsible teacher's plan, so the training should cover the tasks they will actually perform.

Art. 110 certification criteria for evaluation organizations including opportunity for university to object before results
Enforcement Order art. 40: period within seven years for art. 109(2), within five years for art. 109(3)

University Establishment Standards art. 11 (organized training etc.): (1) training for faculty and administrative staff; (2) organized training and research to improve content and methods of classes; (3) training for instructional support staff other than faculty

UES art. 8 basic faculty definition (dedicated or 8+ credits per year) and 8(3) instructional support staff; arts. 13 to 16 qualification routes with educational ability requirement; amendments through MEXT Ordinance No. 29 of 4 September 2026
Graduate School Establishment Standards art. 9-3: parallel training duties, paragraph 2 covers classes and research supervision
CEA is mandatory; 15 certified organizations as of May 2021; NIAD-QE third round of university CEA began 2019 after rounds 2005-2012 and 2012-2019
